endpoints.label: The Home cards: my tasks, my submissions in progress, runs I follow
endpoints.description: tasks { open, overdue, sla_breached, completed_30d, queue } (null without tasks.view_own), submissions { in_progress, completed_30d, submitted_30d } (null without forms.submit), following { active, updated_today, total }. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: My activity over 7, 30 or 90 days: tasks completed, decisions, durations, on time, submissions
endpoints.description: The Home "My activity" charts, computed on the server for the calling person only. period (default 30d) and timezone (day / week buckets; default your profile's time zone, else UTC; 90d uses ISO weeks starting Monday). tasks (null without tasks.view_own): period { days, unit, timezone, start, end }, completed { total, buckets [{ start, count, median_s, p90_s }] }, decisions { total, approved, rejected, returned, approval_rate (approve ÷ decisions; null when none), non_decision, groups [{ kind, label, count }], non_decision_labels }, durations { count, median_s, p90_s, pickup { count, median_s, p90_s } } (assigned → completed / accepted, seconds), on_time { with_deadline, on_time, late, no_deadline, rate } (due date, else the run's SLA), top_processes [{ workflow_id, name, count }]. submissions (null without forms.submit): { total, completed, in_progress, failed, cancelled, no_process, median_s, p90_s } (submitted → process completed). Outcome kinds: approve, reject, return, other (a choice between two or more outcomes), completion (not a decision). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

params.name: timezone
params.description: IANA time zone for day / week buckets, e.g. Pacific/Auckland

endpoints.label: My open tasks with their process and stage
endpoints.description: Open tasks assigned to me that I have accepted or that were added straight to my list (not those still Queued, waiting for my acceptance — see /home/queue). Each has process { workflow_id, name }, stage (the step's name), due_date, overdue, sla_status, priority and assigned_at. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Tasks I can take: waiting for my acceptance, or unassigned in my teams
endpoints.description: The tasks the app's My tasks list shows with status Queued (whether a new task is queued follows the assignee's queue rules). Each has action: accept (POST /tasks/{id}/action with accept) or claim (POST /tasks/{id}/claim). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Forms I submitted, with the process each one started and where it is now
endpoints.description: Newest first. Task-form submissions are task completions and are not listed. Each carries `submission`, the metadata workflows see as {{submission.*}} (reference, submitted_at, submitted_by, form { id, name, version }, source). Each item has status (queued, running, waiting, completed, failed, cancelled, none), status_label ("Waiting on Manager approval"), stages [{ node_id, name, assignees [{ id, name }], team, since, due_date }] (where the run is and who has it) and people (names). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires forms.submit.

params.name: status
params.description: all (default), active (running, waiting or starting), completed, failed (failed or cancelled)

endpoints.label: A run's progress (the submitter-safe flow view)
endpoints.description: For a run you can see (as for following): run { status, status_label, started_at, completed_at, updated_at }, process { name }, flow { nodes (id, type, label, position — no configs), edges, sections, overlay (per-step status) }, stages (where it is now), steps (its tasks: name, status, assignees, team, dates), tasks (its User Tasks with people, history and your per-task can_open / can_act — see GET /workflows/runs/{id}) and submission (when it was your form). Never step configs, outputs, errors, variables or form values. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Workflow runs I follow, with where they are and who has them
endpoints.description: Active runs first, then by last update. Runs I start (form submissions included) are followed automatically unless auto_follow_runs is off (PATCH /home/preferences). Each item has status (queued, running, waiting, completed, failed, cancelled, none), status_label ("Waiting on Manager approval"), stages [{ node_id, name, assignees [{ id, name }], team, since, due_date }] (where the run is and who has it) and people (names). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

params.name: search
params.description: Process name or run title contains

params.name: status
params.description: all (default), active (running, waiting or starting), completed, failed (failed or cancelled)

endpoints.label: Follow a workflow run
endpoints.description: You can follow a run you started, one your form submission started, one you have a task in, or any run with workflows.view_runs (404 otherwise). Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Stop following a workflow run
endpoints.description: Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: My favourite forms (that I can still open), alphabetical
endpoints.description: A favourite is hidden while you cannot open the form (no forms.submit). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Star a form
endpoints.description: Only forms you can open (404 otherwise). Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires forms.submit.

endpoints.label: Unstar a form
endpoints.description: Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: My Home preferences (auto-follow)
endpoints.description: Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Change my Home preferences
endpoints.description: auto_follow_runs (default true): follow the runs you start, form submissions included. Runs already followed stay followed. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: My Home layout in this workspace: widget order, sizes and hidden widgets
endpoints.description: layout { items [{ id, w, h }] (visible widgets in reading order; w = columns of the 12-column desktop grid, h = rows of 40px), hidden [ids] }, customised (false = the default layout), updated_at, grid { columns, row_px, gap_px } and widgets [{ id, title, group, available, default, min, max }]. Widget ids: metric.tasks, chart.decisions, metric.submissions, metric.following, tasks, chart.completed, chart.duration, chart.top_processes, drafts. Stored per person and per workspace; tablets derive their widths from these and phones stack the same order. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Save my Home layout in this workspace
endpoints.description: Replaces the layout. Known widget ids only, each at most once; sizes are clamped to each widget's min / max; widgets you leave out of both items and hidden are put back in their default spot. At most 8192 bytes. Returns the saved layout (as GET). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Reset my Home layout in this workspace to the default
endpoints.description: Other workspaces keep their layouts. Idempotent. Returns the default layout (as GET). Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403).

endpoints.label: Claim an unassigned team task (a member of its team becomes its assignee)
endpoints.description: Atomic: if someone claimed it first, 409. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.complete.

endpoints.label: List tasks
endpoints.description: User-bound credentials only see tasks assigned to (or shared with) their user. `scope=reports` lists the open tasks of the caller's reports instead (the manager view; needs a user and only tasks.view_own), with per-person workload counts in `reports`. Each task carries `unread` (true while it is unread for the credential's person — see PUT /tasks/{id}/read; always false for a credential with no user). Requires tasks.view_all.

params.name: scope
params.description: reports: open tasks of your direct reports (add indirect=true for all levels)

params.name: indirect
params.description: scope=reports: include indirect reports (reports of reports, up to 10 levels)

params.name: sla_breached
params.description: scope=reports: only tasks whose run SLA is breached or whose escalation fired

params.name: strip_html
params.description: Return `description` as plain text (HTML stripped). `description_text` is always included.

endpoints.label: List open tasks assigned to a user or team
endpoints.description: Each task carries `unread` (true while it is unread for the credential's person — see PUT /tasks/{id}/read; always false for a credential with no user). Requires tasks.view_all.

params.name: strip_html
params.description: Return `description` as plain text (HTML stripped). `description_text` is always included.

endpoints.label: Get a task
endpoints.description: Task responses include `description` (as stored: sanitised HTML or plain text) and `description_text` (plain text), and `unread` (true while it is unread for the credential's person — see PUT /tasks/{id}/read; false for a credential with no user). Requires tasks.view_all.

params.name: strip_html
params.description: Return `description` as plain text (HTML stripped). `description_text` is always included.

endpoints.label: Update task fields and User Task field values
endpoints.description: Same field allowlist as the task UI. User-bound credentials only reach their own tasks (and their reports'). Field values of a workflow task are saved by its assignee, or by their manager with on_behalf=true (403 otherwise). Field values of closed tasks cannot change (409). Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: description
params.description: Plain text or HTML. HTML is sanitised to an allowlist (formatting, lists, headings, links, tables, https images); scripts, styles, event handlers and unsafe URLs are removed.

params.name: values
params.description: User Task field values (validated against the task's fields; saved as a draft, required fields are checked on completion)

params.name: on_behalf
params.description: Save a workflow task's values for its assignee (their manager, or tasks.complete_any)

endpoints.label: Accept, hold, reject, complete, escalate or redirect a task
endpoints.description: Workflow tasks are actioned by their assignee only (a member of the assigned team for a team task). Their manager — anyone in the assignee's manager chain in this workspace — may act on behalf with on_behalf=true and an on_behalf_note; the task records actioned_by (the manager) and actioned_on_behalf_of (the assignee) and the assignee is notified. tasks.complete_any (Owner only by default) is the audited break-glass for anyone else, and is required for credentials with no user. 403 otherwise, 404 for another workspace's task, 409 once the task is closed. Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: on_behalf
params.description: Act for the assignee of a workflow task: their manager (anyone in their manager chain), or a holder of tasks.complete_any. Requires on_behalf_note

params.name: on_behalf_note
params.description: Why you are acting on behalf (required with on_behalf; shown to the assignee and recorded in the task history)

endpoints.label: Suggestions for an Autocomplete / lookup field of an open task
endpoints.description: Runs the lookup configured on the task's stored form (data table or API reference) — never a config from the request. The caller must be able to act on the task (user-bound credentials: assignee, collaborator, team member or queue manager). Only the configured columns / fields are returned. Rate limited per user (429). Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: field_key
params.description: Key of an Autocomplete / lookup field of the task's form

params.name: query
params.description: The typed text (matched against the configured search columns / passed to the reference as {{search}})

params.name: values
params.description: The form's current values, for {{task_data.<key>}} placeholders in the lookup's filters or reference inputs

params.name: resolve
params.description: Resolve these stored values to their items (display labels) instead of searching — same source, filters and permissions as a search

params.name: variables
params.description: The form's variables by name ({{var.<name>}}): declared names only, typed and size-bounded; initial values fill the rest

endpoints.label: Rows of a Data table field of an open task (search, filters, sort, page)
endpoints.description: Runs the query stored on the task's form (Data table field) — never a config from the request. The caller must be able to act on the task. Column filters / sorts only on the columns the author allows, ANDed onto the base filter; only the selected columns are returned. Data table sources need data.view unless the author turned on open access. Rate limited per user (429). Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: field_key
params.description: Key of a Data table field of the form

params.name: values
params.description: The form's current values, for {{form.<key>}} in the base filter / API inputs

params.name: params
params.description: Reusable forms: the form's parameters by name ({{param.<name>}} in the base filter / API inputs), re-validated against the declarations; a task form uses the parameters its workflow step passed and ignores these

params.name: variables
params.description: The form's variables by name ({{var.<name>}}): declared names only, typed and size-bounded; initial values fill the rest

endpoints.label: Create a task (with optional subtasks) from an external system
endpoints.description: Create a task (with optional subtasks) from an external system Requires tasks.create.

params.name: description
params.description: Plain text or HTML. HTML is sanitised to an allowlist (formatting, lists, headings, links, tables, https images); scripts, styles, event handlers and unsafe URLs are removed.

endpoints.label: List a task's attachments
endpoints.description: The files on the task's Attachments tab, oldest first, with `can_add` (you can work on the open task), per-attachment `can_delete`, `legal_hold` (the task's form is held: nothing can be deleted), `type_suggestions` and `max_file_bytes`. Visible to the assignee, collaborators, team members, managers of an assignee, the assigner and holders of tasks.view_all / tasks.manage_queue; anyone else gets 404. Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Attach a file to a task (or start a direct upload)
endpoints.description: You must be able to work on the open task (assignee, collaborator, team member, a manager of an assignee, tasks.complete_any, or tasks.manage_queue on a non-workflow task); needs a user-bound credential. With content_base64: the file is checked (size, type by content, blocked types, SVG sanitising, optional virus scan) and attached; returns `{ mode: "uploaded", attachment }`. With size only: `{ mode: "direct", attachment_id, upload: { url, method, headers }, expires_at }` — PUT the bytes to the URL with exactly those headers, then POST /tasks/{id}/attachments/{attachment_id}/complete — or `{ mode: "server", max_bytes }` when the storage can't sign uploads (send content_base64 instead). Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: file_name
params.description: File name (its extension must be an allowed type)

params.name: name
params.description: Display name (default: the file name without its extension)

params.name: type
params.description: Type, free text (default Other). Suggested: Contract, Invoice, Receipt, Evidence, Image, Other

params.name: size
params.description: Size in bytes: without content_base64, starts a direct upload to storage

params.name: content_base64
params.description: The file itself, base64 (small files; the request body limit applies). Omit to get a signed upload URL

endpoints.label: Finish a direct upload of a task attachment
endpoints.description: The uploader only, within the upload window (15 minutes by default), while they can still work on the task. The object is read back and verified; a file that fails is deleted and the reason returned. Requires tasks.complete.

endpoints.label: Delete a task attachment
endpoints.description: The uploader (while they can see the task) or a holder of tasks.delete. Refused (409) while the task's form is on legal hold. The attachment disappears at once; the stored file is purged after TASK_ATTACHMENT_DELETED_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: A short-lived download link for a task attachment
endpoints.description: Returns `{ url, expires_at, attachment }`: a signed link valid for 5 minutes that needs no session (or the plain /attachments/<id> link, which needs a signed-in session, when the instance has no signing key). Every call is written to the audit log. Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Tasks I follow (the Task tracker's Following tab)
endpoints.description: Rows as the Task tracker shows them (assignee, assigner, team, workflow, subtasks, recent_activity, collaborators, assignee_rank, progress_pct) plus followed_at, unread (not opened by you since it became yours) and shared_with_me ({ via: user / team / role, name, invited_by, shared_at } for tasks shared with you by an invite — read only; null otherwise), sorted by due date (none last), then most recently followed. Tasks shared with you (directly, through a team you are in or a role you hold) are listed without following them. Completed tasks stay until you unfollow them (hide_completed=true leaves them out); deleted tasks and tasks you can no longer see drop out. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

params.name: search
params.description: Task name, ID, workflow, people, team, status or priority contains

params.name: hide_completed
params.description: true: leave out completed and cancelled tasks

params.name: shared_only
params.description: true: only tasks shared with you by an invite (read only)

endpoints.label: Follow a task
endpoints.description: You can follow a task you can see: assignee, collaborator, member of the assigned team (unassigned team tasks), a manager of an assignee, the assigner, or tasks.view_all / tasks.manage_queue in its workspace (404 otherwise). Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Stop following a task
endpoints.description: Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Mark a task as read
endpoints.description: What opening the task does in the app. A task you can see; 404 otherwise. Idempotent. A task is unread for you while it is open (todo, in progress or blocked), you hold it (assignee, collaborator or claim candidate, or a member of the assigned team of an unassigned team task) and you have not opened it since it became yours (assigned, reassigned, claimed, or reopened / sent back). Completed, cancelled and draft tasks are never unread. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Mark a task as unread
endpoints.description: Forgets that you opened it. `unread` in the response is the state the rule then gives: a task you don't hold, or a closed one, stays read. A task you can see; 404 otherwise. Idempotent. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Mark all my tasks as read
endpoints.description: Marks every task that is unread for you in the credential's workspace as read; `marked` is how many. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: How many of my tasks are unread
endpoints.description: Top-level tasks that are unread for you in the credential's workspace (the count next to My tasks in the app). A task is unread for you while it is open (todo, in progress or blocked), you hold it (assignee, collaborator or claim candidate, or a member of the assigned team of an unassigned team task) and you have not opened it since it became yours (assigned, reassigned, claimed, or reopened / sent back). Completed, cancelled and draft tasks are never unread. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Who a task is shared with (read only invites)
endpoints.description: The task's invites, oldest first, and can_manage (whether you may invite and remove). Anyone who can see the task reads them; anyone else gets 404. Invite and remove: the assignee or a collaborator, a member of the assigned team, the assigner, a manager of an assignee, a manager of the workflow, or tasks.complete_any (an invited viewer cannot invite others). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Invite people, teams or roles to view a task (read only)
endpoints.description: Shares the task, read only: everyone the invite names (directly, as a member of the team or a holder of the role) can open it (and its subtasks unless include_subtasks is false), its comments, attachments, history and process view, and comment. People invited directly follow it (Task tracker → Following) and get a notification and an email; members of an invited team or role get a notification when it has at most 25 people. Already-invited ones are left as they are. Recorded in the task history and the audit log. Invite and remove: the assignee or a collaborator, a member of the assigned team, the assigner, a manager of an assignee, a manager of the workflow, or tasks.complete_any (an invited viewer cannot invite others). Requires tasks.view_own.

params.name: viewers
params.description: People, teams and roles to invite (at most 50)

params.name: note
params.description: A note for them (shown in the notification)

endpoints.label: Stop sharing a task with a person, team or role
endpoints.description: Removes one invite (its id from GET /tasks/{id}/viewers): its people lose access unless something else lets them see the task, and the follow the invite created is removed. Recorded in the task history and the audit log. Invite and remove: the assignee or a collaborator, a member of the assigned team, the assigner, a manager of an assignee, a manager of the workflow, or tasks.complete_any (an invited viewer cannot invite others). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: List a task's subtasks
endpoints.description: Direct subtasks in order, with `total`, `completed` and `can_add` (whether you may add subtasks here). Visible to anyone who can reach the task (404 otherwise). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Add a subtask
endpoints.description: Title plus optional subtitle, description, estimate, due date, priority and tags. Anyone who can work on the task: tasks.complete and the task within reach — assignee, collaborator, member of its team, the assignee's manager (on their behalf), its assigner / creator, or tasks.view_all (e.g. an admin). Viewers and people who can't reach the task get 403 / 404. Needs a user-bound credential. Workflow tasks included (the subtask is not a workflow task and never completes or resumes the workflow). The subtask goes to the parent's assignee (else you), already accepted, at the end of the list; the parent's progress counts it. 409 when the task is closed; subtasks go at most 4 levels deep. Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: subtitle
params.description: A short summary shown under the title

params.name: description
params.description: Plain text or HTML. HTML is sanitised to an allowlist (formatting, lists, headings, links, tables, https images).

params.name: estimated_effort_minutes
params.description: Estimate in whole minutes (the unit of actual_effort); stored as the creator's estimate. 0 or null = none

endpoints.label: Edit a subtask
endpoints.description: Any of the create fields (only those sent change). Anyone who can work on the task: tasks.complete and the task within reach — assignee, collaborator, member of its team, the assignee's manager (on their behalf), its assigner / creator, or tasks.view_all (e.g. an admin). Viewers and people who can't reach the task get 403 / 404. Needs a user-bound credential. Tick / untick a subtask with PATCH /tasks/{subtaskId} (status) or complete it through POST /tasks/{subtaskId}/action. Requires tasks.complete.

params.name: subtitle
params.description: A short summary shown under the title

params.name: estimated_effort_minutes

params.name: active

params.name: include_logs

endpoints.label: Create a workflow from nodes and edges
endpoints.description: workflows.create is also accepted. A definition fetched from GET /workflows/{id}/definition creates a copy. `warnings` lists wiring problems (references that will be blank, ignored config keys) with suggestions; they never block the save. Requires workflows.edit.

params.name: trigger_config
params.description: Trigger settings, e.g. schedule { cron, timezone }, webhook_received { path, method }, data_table_event { table_id, event_types }

endpoints.description: Get the draft definition in author-payload shape (edit it and send it back to PATCH /workflows/{id}) Requires workflows.view.

endpoints.description: Omitted fields are kept and fields equal to the stored value are not changes (changed: false). Runs keep using the published version until the draft is published. `warnings` lists wiring problems in the saved draft (references that will be blank, ignored config keys) with suggestions; they never block the save. Requires workflows.edit.

params.name: trigger_config
params.description: Trigger settings, e.g. schedule { cron, timezone }, webhook_received { path, method }, data_table_event { table_id, event_types }

endpoints.description: Publish the draft as a new version (runs use it) and activate the workflow Requires workflows.activate.

Keys that are not declared inputs pass through and are listed in `warnings`. Async starts answer 202 with `job_id`. Requires workflows.activate.

params.name: variables
params.description: Input values keyed by input name (GET /workflows/{id}/inputs lists them). Declared inputs are validated and coerced to their type; other keys pass through unchanged.

endpoints.label: Get the input parameters a workflow run accepts
endpoints.description: Fields come from the published version's workflow variables (the draft's when never published; `source` says which). Each field has key, label, type (text, number, boolean, date, datetime, json, select, email, url), required, default, description and options (select). Requires workflows.view.

endpoints.label: Resume a run waiting on an external event
endpoints.description: Resume a run waiting on an external event Requires workflows.activate.

endpoints.label: List workflow runs
endpoints.description: Scoped to the caller (governance): every run with `workflows.view_runs`; with `workflows.view_queue` only runs the caller is involved in (started it, their form submission started it, or they have a task in it) plus every run of workflows they hold an explicit View grant on. Requires workflows.view_queue.

Scoped to the caller (governance): every run with `workflows.view_runs`; with `workflows.view_queue` only runs the caller is involved in (started it, their form submission started it, or they have a task in it) plus every run of workflows they hold an explicit View grant on. Requires workflows.view_queue.

endpoints.label: Pause, resume or cancel a run

endpoints.label: List queued workflow jobs

The content is the published version; with version=draft (forms.edit) the working draft's content instead, when there is one (content says which). Editors also get draft: who last saved the draft and when, or null. Form drafts: a form has a published version (what everyone sees: form pages, start forms, the Forms menu, public links, task forms, workflow drafts and test runs, GET /forms/{id}) and at most one working draft, shared by every editor (forms.edit). The draft records who saved it last and when, and the version it started from (base_version).
